text:
maria: Heads up — I rotated an IAM binding for the SAST/DAST scanner service account a few mins ago (scanner-sa). After the change I'm seeing intermittent 403s from the CI runner when it tries to decrypt scan artifacts with KMS. Not sure if audit logs got lost during the role flip.

cheng: @maria can you paste the exact commands you ran? also which project/keystore?

maria: ran this (shortened):
```
# removed creds, real command was run in org project
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-infra --member=serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Keystore: projects/redwood-infra/locations/global/keyRings/scan-keys/cryptoKeys/scan-decrypt-key

samir: seeing same in CI: a few SAST jobs failed with: `KMS: PermissionDenied` then later succeeded after requeue. Looks like some requests hit old binding cache.

devops-bot: deployment-notice: IAM binding change applied by maria via infra-ci (run id: infra-8821).

olivia: :eyes: ok can we confirm audit log entries for the rebind? i'm worried there's a gap for a 5-10m window that would make triage harder if we need to trace who accessed what.

maria: checked Audit Logs -> Admin Activity and Data Access: I can see the `SetIamPolicy` call at 1769001227 but there are two KMS `Decrypt` attempts at 1769001255 that are missing detailed proto payloads (just a generic status).

cheng: suggests: check if keystore has CMEK rotation or grant propagation latency. Also run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy ...` to confirm binding present. if we still see gaps, we should preserve the CI job logs and open a support case (or file internal incident).

samir: quick repro I ran locally — first `gradle scan` hit 403 decrypt, retried after 8s succeeded. logs: `rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor not authorized` then `OK`. Could be transient IAM cache on KMS side.

maria: filed internal ticket SEC-2026-814 with attachments (job logs, audit snippets). adding more context to the ticket now.

tara: we should treat this as a scan pipeline outage candidate. action items: preserve all related CI artifacts (done?), tag runs for later eval, add temporary canary to detect KMS 403s, and draft comms to teams relying on scan results.

olivia: i'm +1 for runbook invocation if we see >5% scan failures in the last 30m. @devops-bot can you add alert rule: `scan.pipeline.kms.decrypt_errors >= 5%` to the SLO dashboard?

devops-bot: alert-rule-create: `scan.pipeline.kms.decrypt_errors` created (threshold 5%, lookback 30m).

cheng: one more thing — check scanner SA tokens. If the SA was momentarily removed and then re-added we might have a token TTL issue for long-lived runners. let's rotate short-lived tokens and prefer workload identity where possible.

maria: confirmed all artifacts for the affected runs are preserved in GCS path: gs://redwood-ci/scan-artifacts/17690012*/. Uploading additional executor debug logs to SEC-2026-814.

samir: on triage — we saw ~7 failed SAST jobs in the window, 3 DAST runs reported `404` on auth endpoint because token exchange failed. probably downstream effect. marking those as potential false positives until we re-run.

olivia: next steps I assigned: 1) keep SEC-2026-814 open until we get KMS audit payload clarity (maria), 2) run backfilled scans for any PRs that had failing scans (samir), 3) add an RBAC change checklist to infra PRs to notify security and create an ephemeral trace (tara).

maria: created PR with checklist template: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/ops/compare/iam-change-checklist — includes `pre-change: notify-sec`, `post-change: preserve-audit-window`, `verify: run sample decrypt`.

tara: nice. also propose a short postmortem note in #incidents if we confirm this caused any blocked releases. keep it high-level.

cheng: forensics note: if the KMS audit payloads are incomplete, we can use GKE/node-level logs and the CI executor traces to reconstruct requestor identities. not fun but doable.

maria: FYI I also checked GCP Support — opened ticket case 2026-9001 requesting payload retention/backfill for the 1769001225-1769001300 window.

samir: re-run started for the 3 affected PRs. I'll post results here when complete.

olivia: thanks all — update the ticket with re-run hashes and we'll decide if this becomes a formal incident after results. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: incident-candidate: severity=medium, related_ticket=SEC-2026-814, linked_case=2026-9001, owner=maria

maria: logging final note — this one felt like IAM propagation/cache latency + a brief role flip. adding a mitigation suggestion to the checklist: `pause CI or drain scanner workers during IAM flips` to avoid mid-window failures.

cheng: agreed. also add a monitoring probe that does a `kms.decrypt` smoke check immediately after policy changes.

maria: will add both to PR. thanks everyone.
